newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE to crawl to 4,325 after dull start.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE to crawl to 4,325 after dull start.

text.p: After a dull start by the London stock market which may take the FTSE 100 index down to touch 4,305, it should manage to crawl up towards 4,325 on Friday, technical analysts said.

Market bulls have been given a reprieve after having been mauled recently and unless investor fears concerning interest rates resurface later today the bears will fail to capitalise very much further on the fragile state of the market.
As a result, the market will be in a fairly relaxed mood waiting for the opportunity to nudge higher.
By 0808 GMT, the FTSE was indicated up 1.4 at 4,314.6
Thursday's action by the FTSE indicated confidence returning to the market because it finished at the day's high after having sunk below the previous day's low.
Other factors which give weight for move up today include readings of the put/call ratio for FTSE index options, analysts said.

This ratio had been as high as five-to-one on Wednesday and since this is normally used as a contrary indicator an extremely high reading is deemed bullish or that the market is near to making a turn for the better.

This is because the bears will have been actively trading puts in the hope the market will fall but once this pressure has been satisfied, put activity dwindles giving rise to more calls being traded as market sentiment swings the other way.

On Thursday, the put/call ratio reduced to evens. But the bears have not been seen off completely and the fear of an interest rise in the U.S. perhaps later in the day will send the FTSE down on its knees again but for the moment, having re-estabished a footing above 4,300, the seal is set for the market's short-term survival, analysts said.
